members.title: Precinct | Urban Planners in Toowoomba
members.description: Precinct Urban Planning is a boutique town planning consultancy practice offering specialist services in statutory and strategic planning and development management. Based in the dynamic western growth corridor, with offices in Toowoomba and Ipswich
members.intro: Formed in 2002, Precinct Urban Planning is a boutique town planning consultancy practice offering specialist services in statutory and strategic planning and development management. Based in the dynamic western growth corridor, with offices in Toowoomba and Ipswich, Precinct Urban Planning services public and private sector clients throughout Queensland and New South Wales. The practice offers specialist technical expertise in a number of areas to assist with developments of all sizes and at all stages.

body.text: Company Bio

Precinct Urban Planning personnel have extensive experience in strategic, statutory and specialist town planning and management consulting services and provide timely, accurate and strategically astute advice focussed on individual client needs. The practice values experience, provides insight and delivers workable planning solutions.
Personal Bio

James is a qualified town planner, having completed a Bachelor of Planning degree at James Cook University (JCU) in Townsville, North Queensland, graduating in 2018. His studies involved a number of practical courses including Indigenous Environmental Management, Environmental and Regional Planning, and Urban Design.

James has over seven (7) years’ experience within the private sector. Prior to joining Precinct Urban Planning in early 2019, James previously worked as a Planner for a building certification company in Townsville. In addition to assessing proposed developments in rural and regional Queensland against the relevant planning requirements, this position also allowed him to understand and implement building legislation, such as the Building Act 1975 and Queensland Development Code.

Since becoming a member of the Precinct team, James has gained a wealth of knowledge and experience, working on a range of developments from small-scale uses such as Airbnbs, dwellings and offices to large-scale uses such as poultry farms, schools, hospitals and community facilities. He has also benefitted by assisting local governments in the assessment of various types of Development Applications.

In these roles, James has developed the knowledge to provide accurate and succinct planning advice for an array of residential, commercial, industrial and rural projects in a range of council regions across Queensland, New South Wales and Western Australia.

Additionally, James has worked on projects of regional and state significance, including Ministerial and Local Government Infrastructure Designations for the redevelopment of the Toowoomba Hospital and other large scale projects such as hospitals, schools, electricity infrastructure and dams.

articles.title: What a Day! TRG Charity Golf Day 2025 Wrap-Up
articles.description: Our annual Charity Golf Day was nothing short of incredible. From the first tee-off to the final putt, the day was packed with laughs, generosity, community spirit, and (let’s be honest) a few creative golf swings.

body.text: If you’ve ever heard whispers that the Toowoomba Referral Group Charity Golf Day is something special, consider this your confirmation.

Our annual Charity Golf Day was nothing short of incredible. From the first tee-off to the final putt, the day was packed with laughs, generosity, community spirit, and (let’s be honest) a few creative golf swings.
The Big Result
Thanks to the overwhelming support of our sponsors, golfers, volunteers, and donors, we’re proud to share that we raised an incredible:
$32,803.70 for charity
Not only did we beat last year’s total, we absolutely smashed it.
All funds raised will be shared evenly between two very deserving charities:
Hope Horizons
Maddox’s Helping Hand Foundation
These funds will make a genuine, tangible difference in the lives of individuals and families in our community, and we couldn’t be more grateful to everyone who played a part.
More Than Just a Game of Golf
While the golf itself was… entertaining (accuracy was optional), the real highlight of the day was the atmosphere.
From generous sponsors and prize donors to volunteers who kept everything running smoothly, and golfers who brought the fun and the heart, the TRG community showed up in the best possible way.
It was a reminder of what can happen when local businesses and individuals come together with a shared purpose: to give back, support those who need it most, and enjoy the process along the way.
Thank You
To every sponsor, donor, golfer, volunteer, and supporter — thank you. Your generosity, energy, and willingness to get involved are what make this event bigger and better every year.
You are truly the best team we’ve ever teed up with.
Want to Be Part of Next Year’s Event?
If you missed out this year — or you’re already keen to do it all again — now’s the time to get ahead of the crowd.
Expressions of Interest are now open for:
Sponsorship opportunities

articles.title: TRG Guest: Jesse McCartney from Belong in Hockey
articles.description: TRG was inspired to hear from Jessie McCartney, co-founder of award-winning initiative Belong in Hockey — a Toowoomba program using sport to support refugees and build community connections.

body.text: Belong in Hockey. Sport, Community, and a Whole Lot of Heart
We were delighted to welcome Jessie McCartney to our Wednesday morning meeting to share the story behind Belong in Hockey. And what a story it is.

Belong in Hockey is an award-winning, Toowoomba-based initiative founded by Jessie and Elizabeth Laverty that uses the power of sport to support refugees, particularly Yazidi families, as they settle into life in our community. Through weekly training sessions — now expanded to include Saturdays — the program builds far more than hockey skills. It fosters confidence, community connection, and even English proficiency along the way.

It's the kind of initiative that reminds you just how much a simple game can change lives. Jessie's passion for the people behind the program was infectious, and it's no surprise that Belong in Hockey has earned award recognition for the incredible work they do.
We left the meeting feeling genuinely inspired by what Jessie and Elizabeth have built right here in Toowoomba.
If you would like more information regarding the program, please email Jessie, the Hockey Manager, at hockeymanager@toowoombahockey.com.au

articles.title: TRG GUEST: Jules from Hope for Our Children
articles.description: TRG was honoured to welcome Jules Davey, CEO of Hope for Our Children, to our Wednesday morning meeting. Hear about their incredible Bags of Hope program and how TRG is proud to support their vital work in Toowoomba.

body.text: A morning that pulled at our heartstrings
We were so honoured to have Jules Davey, CEO of Hope for Our Children, join us for a cuppa and a chat at our Wednesday morning meeting.
There wasn't a dry eye in the house as Jules spoke about the incredible work Hope for Our Children does, in particular, their Bags of Hope program.

Imagine being taken from the place you call home and sent somewhere unfamiliar, with nothing. That's exactly what Bags of Hope works to address. Providing vulnerable children with essential items to restore their dignity and inspire hope for a brighter future.

TRG was proud to donate $1,000 to this amazing cause. As a non-government funded organisation, Hope for Our Children relies entirely on grants and community support, so every single dollar truly counts.
If you'd like to learn more or support their work, visit hopeforourchildren.com.au.

articles.title: Toowoomba’s Own Kevin Howarth Rings Out Success at the Australian Town Crier Championships
articles.description: Australia’s Loudest Crier is from Toowoomba! Kevin Howarth takes home four major awards, showcasing his dedication and pride in the local community.

body.text: Toowoomba’s very own Town Crier and valued Toowoomba Referral Group (TRG) member, Kevin Howarth, has once again proven that passion and pride go hand in hand — and that his voice carries further than most!

At the 36th National Town Crier Championships held in Canberra, Kevin delivered a standout performance, taking home four national titles, including Australia’s Loudest Crier, Best Cry, Best Media Campaign, and the prestigious Pat Adamson Memorial Award for Best Regional Ambassador.

Despite challenging conditions — with gusty winds toppling shade shelters and sending tricorn hats flying — Kevin’s dedication and spirit shone through. “I’ve competed in many events over the years, but Canberra’s wind made this one particularly memorable,” Kevin said with a grin.“Crying into the wind was tricky for everyone, but the effort was worth it. The job satisfaction I get from representing Toowoomba and sharing our story with others is incredible.”

Kevin’s “loudest cry” reached 92 decibels on the day — slightly below his usual competition level of over 100 decibels, but still strong enough to defend his title for another year. He previously claimed the same honour in 2018, 2019, and 2023.

As the Toowoomba Region’s official Town Crier, Kevin proudly represents the community at events big and small — from citizenship ceremonies and centenarian birthdays to major festivals and civic celebrations. His booming voice, warm personality, and genuine pride in Toowoomba have made him a much-loved local figure. Toowoomba Regional Council Mayor Cr Geoff McDonald congratulated Kevin on his outstanding success, commending his enthusiasm and commitment.

“We know Kevin gives 100% at every competition and every appearance he makes,” Mayor McDonald said.“These awards are a well-deserved recognition of his effort and energy. Kevin’s humour, warmth and community spirit make him a fantastic Ambassador for the Toowoomba Region — and now he has the Australian titles to match.

”A proud member of the Toowoomba Referral Group, Kevin brings the same energy and positivity to the group’s meetings and community initiatives as he does to the national stage. His commitment to promoting local pride and supporting fellow Toowoomba professionals makes him an outstanding representative both within TRG and across Australia.

Fresh from Canberra, Kevin’s calendar remains packed. He recently made his traditional appearance at the Toowoomba Carnival of Flowers Grand Central Floral Parade, welcomed guests at a Brisbane 2032 Olympic Games organising committee civic reception, and has a host of community events lined up in the months ahead.
Congratulations, Kevin — and thank you for continuing to represent both Toowoomba and the Toowoomba Referral Group with pride, passion, and plenty of volume!

aboutBlocks.text: Toowoomba Referral Group is a business referral group which focuses on providing business networking and business leads within a structured and positive environment.
TRG is a registered Not for Profit Incorporated Association (IA55093) that organises business networking meetings every Wednesday from 9am to 10am for members and invited guests.
Each member is given the opportunity to promote their business. Guest and motivational speakers from a range of professions are regularly organised to present to the group.

communityBlocks.text: TRG’s Ongoing Support for the Toowoomba Community

TRG has long been a proud supporter of the Toowoomba region, investing time, resources, and expertise to help the community thrive. From sponsoring local events and sporting clubs to collaborating with schools and charities, TRG takes an active role in creating opportunities that strengthen the city’s social and economic fabric.
Their involvement goes beyond business—it’s about fostering connections and supporting the people who make Toowoomba such a vibrant place to live and work.

Through partnerships with local organisations, TRG champions initiatives that drive education, sustainability, and innovation. Whether it’s contributing to community development projects, backing local entrepreneurs, or supporting youth programs, TRG continually seeks to make a lasting difference. Their focus on empowering local talent and nurturing future leaders reflects a deep belief in Toowoomba’s potential and resilience.

TRG’s ongoing presence in the Toowoomba community demonstrates their unwavering commitment to giving back. By aligning their values with the needs of the region, they continue to build meaningful relationships and contribute to a stronger, more connected community.
As Toowoomba continues to grow, TRG remains dedicated to playing its part—investing in people, supporting local success, and helping shape a brighter future for generations to come.

golfBlocks.text: The TRG Charity Golf Day is an annual community event hosted by the Toowoomba Referral Group to raise funds for two local charities.
Held at the picturesque Toowoomba Golf Club, it’s a day where local businesses, sponsors, and players come together for a round of golf, good food, and great company — all for a worthy cause.

With team registrations, hole sponsorships, and prizes throughout the day, the eventblends friendly competition with genuine community spirit, helping make adifference for local families affected by cancer and serious injury.
